author: TEDx Talks
description:
Many people know Carol Hutchins as the winningest coach in the history of NCAA Softball and Michigan Athletics, but few know that her storied journey was filled with challenges that were and still are shared by all of women’s sports. Carol’s speech takes us through the happenings in the post-Title IX era that transformed the story of women’s sports from one of underrepresentation, underinvestment, and undervaluation to one of opportunity, achievement, and acceptance, as women moved beyond tomboy labels to become dominant leaders on and off the field. 

I am Carol Hutchins, or Coach Hutch to most anyone who knows me. I have spent my entire adult life in college.  I was the Head Softball coach at UM for 38 years, and have been here now for 44 years.  I coached championship teams on the field, but I actually coached championship people, by teaching them that excellence is harder than average, and anything less than excellence is not acceptable. Not just on the field, but IN LIFE.

title: How Title IX changed women's sports | Carol Hutchins | TEDxUofM

description: How different will the world be just ten years from now? Physicist, entrepreneur, and technology researcher Alex Wissner-Gross argues that artificial intelligence is accelerating humanity toward one of the greatest transformations in history. From solving previously impossible mathematical problems and curing diseases to advancing robotics, space exploration, and scientific discovery, he believes AI will fundamentally reshape civilization far sooner than most people expect. In this wide-ranging conversation, Wissner-Gross explores superintelligence, the future of consciousness, human enhancement, extraterrestrial life, and why data—not algorithms—has been the true engine behind AI's rapid progress. He also explains why the choices we make today could determine whether the next decade becomes humanity's greatest leap forward. Dr. Alexander D. Wissner-Gross is a physicist, computer scientist, entrepreneur, and investor working at the intersection of artificial intelligence and the physi
title: The Next 10 Years of AI Will Change Everything  | Alexander Wissner-Gross | TEDxBoston

author: TEDx Talks
description: Will AI destroy jobs—or unlock an era of unprecedented prosperity? MIT principal research scientist and bestselling author Andy McAfee challenges some of today's biggest assumptions about artificial intelligence. Rather than fearing an AI-driven job apocalypse, he argues that AI will expand human capability, fuel entrepreneurship, improve healthcare, lower costs, and create new opportunities for innovation. In this thought-provoking conversation with John Werner, McAfee explores why optimism may be the most rational response to rapid technological change, what businesses must do to adapt, and why the next decade could bring extraordinary improvements in both economic prosperity and human flourishing. Andrew McAfee is a scientist at MIT, cofounder of the generative AI company Workhelix, and the inaugural visiting fellow in the Technology and Society group at Google. His work investigates how digital technologies are changing the world, and what kinds of companies are best able to lead
title: The Optimistic Case for AI | Andrew McAfee | TEDxBoston

description:
What keeps us going? Lianzheng offers a heartfelt answer through his own story: perseverance is never about struggling alone—it is a relay of love, trust, and personal growth.

From a factory worker to a national marathon athlete, he has pursued his dreams with his wife by his side, serving as both his safe harbor and his catalyst. When he was exhausted, she offered acceptance; when he hesitated, she gave him confidence. Over time, her simple words—"I believe in you"—became the voice within himself.

When support from others gradually grows into inner conviction, we ultimately gain the strength to face life's challenges.

Each of us can become the "engineer" of our own lives.

坚持，到底靠什么？大正用自己的故事给出了一个温暖的答案：坚持不是一个人的苦撑，而是一场关于爱、信任与自我成长的接力。
从机械厂工人到马拉松国家健将，他一路追梦的背后始终有妻子作为他的“避风港”和“催化剂”——在疲惫时给予接纳，在犹豫时给予坚定。一句句“我相信你”最终内化成为他心底的声音。
当外界的支持慢慢生长为内心的信念，我们也终将拥有面对困难的力量。

description: Why are we often kinder to strangers than we are to ourselves? Through personal stories of academic pressure, failure, rejection, and unexpected second chances, this talk explores the psychological trap of believing that everyone is watching and judging our mistakes. Drawing on the "spotlight effect," Ky Anh reveals how the harshest critic is often ourselves - and how letting go of imagined judgment can help us embrace imperfection, recover from setbacks, and move forward with greater confidence. Before returning to Vietnam, I studied at Anglo-Chinese School (Independent) in Singapore on a full scholarship, where much of my identity revolved around academic achievement and the pressure to be “perfect.” That experience shaped how I viewed mistakes, success, and self-worth. In my TEDx talk, I reflect on moments when things didn’t go according to plan, from academic setbacks to awkward classroom slips, and how those experiences challenged my fear of being judged. Con honestidad y fortaleza, demuestra que los límites pueden transformarse en oportunidades cuando se enfrentan con determinación, amor y esperanza. Al mismo tiempo, rinde un profundo reconocimiento al apoyo incondicional de su familia, cuyo acompañamiento ha sido fundamental en su camino. Una charla que nos recuerda que nadie alcanza sus metas solo y que el amor, la resiliencia y la confianza pueden abrir caminos que parecían imposibles. Mary Chao es conferencista, creadora de contenido e impulsora de la inclusión y la diversidad. A través de su historia personal ha inspirado a miles de personas a replantear la manera en que perciben la discapacidad, demostrando que las verdaderas barreras suelen estar en los prejuicios y no en las personas.

Con autenticidad, sensibilidad y un profundo sentido del humor, Mary comparte experiencias que invitan a desar

En s’appuyant sur la psychologie et la pédagogie, Vanessa déconstruit le mythe de la résilience innée : elle n'est pas un muscle, mais un lien de confiance. Un talk inspirant qui redéfinit notre rôle de parents et d’éducateurs pour aider une génération à naviguer dans la tempête. Mère de deux adolescents et enseignante à l’école Selwyn House depuis 21 ans, Vanessa Jothy a enrichi sa pédagogie en passant des arts plastiques à la première année. description:
40年間で2,800冊を世に送り出してきた出版プロデューサー・吉田浩さんが、読書が持つ「人生を変える力」を紐解きます。

読書は、健康寿命を延ばし、収入を上げ、ストレスを軽減する――。幼少期に患った重い心臓病を「本」に救われた自身のエピソードを交えながら、読解力が人生のさまざまな課題を解決する土台になることを語ります。

AIが台頭し、情報が一瞬で消費されていく現代において、本を読み、感情を揺さぶられることは、人間にしかできない特権です。

今夜、あなたはどんな本を開きますか？

Publishing producer Hiroshi Yoshida, who has brought 2,800 books into the world over the past 40 years, explores the life-changing power of reading.

Reading can help us live longer, healthier lives, increase our income, and reduce stress. Drawing on his own experience of being saved by books while battling a serious heart condition in childhood, Yoshida explains how reading comprehension provides the foundation for solving the many challenges we encounter throughout life.

In an age when AI is rapidly advancing and information is consumed in an instant, opening a book and allowing ourselves to be emotionally moved is a privilege unique to human beings.

What book will you open tonight? 童話作家、出版プロデューサー。
1960年、新潟県六日町生まれ。法政大学卒。青山学院大学大学院卒。
吉田浩氏が執筆した童
title: 本を読む人は幸せになれる　Why Reading Makes Us Happier | Hiroshi Yoshida 吉田浩 | TEDxMarunouchi
